title: Al-Ghaniyy, the Self-Sufficient
tomorrow: rich, or content? why does one verse put the two side by side?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Jami', and a wall that gathered people who'd never have stood in one place. The line: he gathers. Today, a king, a throne, and a thank you.
screen: `HE GATHERS.` → `A KING, A THRONE, A THANK YOU.`

segments.voice: Dadi prays every day, again and again, to a God the Qur'an says needs nothing at all. That was yesterday's question, and a king holds the answer. Solomon, Sulayman in Arabic, is in his court. He asks who can bring him the throne of the queen of Sheba, from far away. One says: before you rise from your seat. Then someone with knowledge of the Book says: before your gaze returns to you. Solomon looks. And the throne is standing right there in front of him. What does a king say when the impossible just arrived?
screen: `A GOD WHO NEEDS NOTHING.` → `THE QUEEN OF SHEBA'S THRONE.` → `BEFORE YOUR GAZE RETURNS.`

segments.voice: Not "look what I did." In the Qur'an's telling, Solomon says this is from the bounty of his Lord, a test of whether he'll be grateful. Then he adds the part that answers Dadi's question. Whoever gives thanks gives it for the good of his own soul, and whoever is ungrateful, his Lord is free of need and generous. That's today's Name. Al-Ghaniyy, the Self-Sufficient, needing nothing. Another verse says it to everyone, in Pickthall's words: "O mankind! Ye are the poor in your relation to Allah. And Allah! He is the Absolute, the Owner of Praise." So the prayer isn't a payment that keeps the world running. There's a hadith qudsi, words the Prophet, peace be upon him, gave as from God, that says if every person who ever lived, first to last, had the heart of the most devout among them, it would add nothing to His kingdom. Here's the thing to tell a friend tonight: in Solomon's own words, thanks is for the soul that gives it. Dadi's prayers don't fill a need in God. They do something in Dadi.
screen: `THIS IS FROM THE BOUNTY OF MY LORD.` · `THANKS IS FOR YOUR OWN SOUL.` · `YE ARE THE POOR. HE IS THE ABSOLUTE.` · `NOT A PAYMENT.` · then, large: `HE NEEDS NOTHING.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and set down the feeling of owing a performance. Nothing you bring to the next two minutes is needed by anyone. Simply breathe, and notice what a sit feels like when it isn't a payment.
Al-Ghaniyy. The Self-Sufficient: needing nothing from us, which is why every thank you lands back on the one who gives it.
Here's one for the pocket: he needs nothing, so your thanks is a gift to your own soul. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims describe prayer as worship offered for God's sake that, in the Qur'an's words, is for the good of the worshipper's own soul.

original.note: Arabic: the Self-Sufficient, a Name of Allah; Pickthall renders it 'the Absolute' in 35:15.

trapdoor: what you thought: a God too far above to care.
what it means: He needs nothing, so nothing we give is a payment, and what we give comes back to us.
what a scholar hears: 27:40 (thanks for one's own soul), 35:15 (ye are the poor), and the hadith qudsi in Sahih Muslim 2577.
guess: the Rich One, owner of all gold
the Distant One, too far to care

chat.says: Eli asked why we pray if God 'doesn't need it.' i said 'because.' he looked so unimpressed
options: Give him the Qur'an's answer: God needs nothing. The thanks is for our own good.
Tell him God does need it, or He'd be lonely without our prayers.
Tell him prayer is a payment, so God keeps sending the good stuff.
chat.meaning: Al-Ghaniyy needs nothing. In the Qur'an, Solomon says whoever gives thanks gives it for the good of his own soul.

Al-Ghaniyy.meaning: the Self-Sufficient; a Name of Allah

Sulayman.meaning: Solomon, a prophet and king in the Qur'an

Sheba.meaning: a kingdom ruled by a queen in the story

hadith qudsi.meaning: words the Prophet gave as from God, outside the Qur'an
